nodes.text: State: information identified by the applicable contract.
Operation: work that can read or change working state.
Exception: an execution event transferred to an applicable exception response.
Boundary: declared execution extent across which a property is required.
Survival: availability of the contract-selected state across the required boundary.
Responsibility: a contract's assignment of a behavior to a role.
Sentinel: a distinguished value or state with a declared interpretation.
Contract: scoped requirements, bindings and permitted behavior.
The required JSON state must survive an exception.
The surrounding system owns exception handling.
Exception-handling responsibility is not assigned to the JSON handler.
Error is a valid sentinel-state category.
Exception is a valid sentinel-state category.

S is the exact caller-supplied valid JSON text; T extends from entry into system_run through its return. The caller retains S. Working state is parsed separately. Input gates are READY or ERROR. ERROR skips decoding and operation. COMPLETE reports normal return. EXCEPTION reports an ordinary Exception caught by system_run. The response requirement is catching and returning the declared report. Partial working state and external effects have no preservation guarantee here.
For L01, preserve S across T and assign exception response to the system, with declared error/exception representations.
Bind S and T; preserve S separately; apply the gate; decode and invoke only on READY; respond to ordinary exceptions in the system; assess preservation and response separately.
If an applicable contract requires survival of S across T and adequate evidence establishes loss of that same S across that same T, its preservation obligation is unmet.
conditions: The preservation contract applies to the examined operation.
The selected survivor S and required boundary T are identified.
Adequate evidence establishes loss of that same S across that same T.
nodes.conclusion: That contract's preservation obligation is unmet.
